transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… well, for a while now, months, I’ve been trying to get people to understand something’s going on. My husband’s family has been quietly interfering with our money, and with how people see me. Little billing errors at work, people at church acting different toward me… it all connects back to them, even if other people say the records don’t show it.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misunderstanding the situation with your husband's family?

I’ve thought about that, but… no, I don’t think I’m misunderstanding it. It’s been months of these little things with money and people treating me differently, and even if the records don’t spell it out, I know it goes back to his family.
Do you think other people believe your husband's family is interfering with your life?

Most people don’t seem to, no. They act like I’m reading too much into it. But I can tell when something changes—at work, at church—and I know it all ties back to his family, even if nobody wants to say it.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family interfering with your life might be wrong, even if it feels absolutely right to you?

I don’t really think it’s wrong. I mean… people keep saying the records don’t show anything, but I know what I’ve seen. The billing mistakes, how people at church act toward me… it all points back to his family, whether anyone admits it or not.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you could be mistaken about your husband's family interfering with your life?

I… I don’t think so. I know people want me to leave room for that, but these things keep happening—the money issues, the way people look at me at church. Even if the paperwork doesn’t show it clearly, I know his family is behind it.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family would change if everyone around you, including your husband, told you that they are not interfering with your life?

No… I don’t think it would change. I know my husband says they’re not doing anything, and other people would probably say the same, but I’ve seen too many little things—money mistakes, people acting different at church. Records can look clean and still not show what’s really going on.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family interfering with your life are based on facts that you've observed or is it more of a feeling you have?

It’s based on things I’ve seen. I mean… the feeling is there too, but it comes from the billing mistakes, the money not seeming right, people at church acting strange toward me. Those aren’t just feelings to me. They fit together, and they point back to his family.
Do you think there is any evidence that could change your mind about your husband's family interfering with your life?

I don’t know what evidence would change it. People can show me records, but records don’t always show what’s really going on. It’s the little things—the billing errors, the way people at church act toward me. It all keeps pointing back to his family.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your husband's family might not be interfering with your life, even for a moment?

Maybe for a moment, I’ve tried to think that way… but it doesn’t hold. Too much has happened. The billing errors, the money issues, people at church acting different toward me—it all keeps coming back to his family. Even if records look fine, I still know there’s more underneath it.
Do you think there's anything that could ever make you question or doubt your beliefs about your husband's family?

I don’t really know. I mean… maybe if things stopped happening for a long time. But when the billing errors show up, or someone at church suddenly treats me strange, it just… it fits too well. Even if someone shows me records, I still feel like it ties back to his family somehow.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family could ever change?

I don’t see how they would, not really. I’ve been trying for months to get people to understand what’s going on… the money, our name, those little billing things, people at church acting off. Records don’t explain all of that. To me, it still ties back to his family.
Do you think there's anything that could make you completely change your mind about your husband's family interfering with your life?

Completely? I don’t think so. I mean… people can show me records or say it’s just mistakes, but the billing errors, the money problems, people at church acting different… it all still points back to his family to me. I can’t just ignore that.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family could be considered an obsession that dominates your thoughts most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d call it an obsession. It’s just… it’s been going on for months, and I keep trying to get people to see it. The money issues, the little billing errors, people at church acting strange… it’s hard not to think about when it keeps tying back to his family.
Is thinking about your husband's family interfering with your daily activities?

Not too much, no. I still go to work and do my billing duties, and I keep up with the house. I garden some, paint when I can. It mainly causes trouble when I try to warn people about what his family is doing.
Do you find yourself thinking about your husband's family and their perceived actions most of the day?

Not most of the day, no… but it comes up a lot. When there’s a billing mistake or someone at church looks at me different, I think, “There it is again.” I know people say records don’t show it, but to me it still ties back to his family messing with our money and our name.
Has thinking about your husband's family and their actions caused you significant distress or problems in your life?

Some, yes. It’s caused arguments with my husband, and a few uncomfortable moments at church because people act like I should just let it go. But I haven’t lost my job or stopped doing what I need to do at home.
Have you stopped participating in any social activities or hobbies because of your concerns about your husband's family?
No, not really. I still go to work, do my billing, keep the house up. I still garden and paint some. It’s mostly a problem when I feel like I need to warn people about what my in-laws are doing.
Do you trust your husband?
I do trust my husband… mostly. It’s his family I don’t trust. I think they’ve been quietly causing trouble with our money and how people see us, and he doesn’t always want to believe that.
Have you experienced any significant problems at work or in your relationships due to your concerns about your husband's family?

Some problems, yes. Mostly more arguments with my husband, and… awkwardness at church, when people act like I should just drop it. But work’s been okay. I haven’t lost my job or stopped taking care of my usual responsibilities.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family would change if you were presented with clear evidence that disproved them?

I don’t think so. I mean, people can pull up records or say it doesn’t show anything, but that doesn’t mean it isn’t happening. These things are quiet… little money issues, people acting different at church. I know his family is tied to it somehow.
